abstract.para: After a disaster occurs, boot the &rear; recovery system and start the recovery installer on a machine with identical hardware to the original machine. The following procedure refers to this new machine as the replacement machine. Technically, the replacement machine could be a tested, identical machine that replaces the original machine, or it could be the original machine after replacing any broken hardware.

listitem.para: A recovery system was created on the original machine.
The recovery system is available on a bootable recovery medium.
The replacement machine has identical hardware to the original machine.
The replacement storage is clean and as-new. This might mean never-used new storage or existing storage that is completely wiped. For more information, see

topic.para: Perform this procedure on the replacement machine:

step.para: If necessary, replace any broken hardware.
Boot the replacement machine from the recovery medium.
Log in as &rootuser;. No password is needed.
Start the recovery installer, using the -D option to enable debugscript mode:
This command performs the following steps:

listitem.para: Restores the disk layout, including partitions, file systems and mount points.
Restores the system files and user files from the backup.

important.title: Using debugscript mode might log secrets
important.para: Using debugscript mode provides the most debugging information, including logging commands and arguments in the &rear; log file. However, secrets and sensitive information might also be logged. Make sure you remove or obscure this information before sharing the log file.

step.para: After the recovery process is finished, reboot the system:

Log in to the restored system with the original credentials. Check whether the system was successfully re-created and can serve as a replacement for the original machine in the production environment.
If the checks are successful, add the replacement machine back to the production environment.
